subject: FitShot discovery recap & eval pack + pinning options
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Patel <nora@fitshot.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 05 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: FitShot discovery recap & next steps

Hi Nora — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and tangible next steps so we all have the same plan: 

Summary (2 min):
- FitShot is focused on real-time freight ETA normalization and exceptions classification (short text inputs, many partials).
- Primary constraints: 10–50ms per inference target for UI, bursty spikes around end-of-day, and strict PII handling for driver IDs.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) We’ll share an "eval pack" with recommended model profiles, a curated prompt set (sanitized), and a benchmark spreadsheet so you can run against your sample corpus. (See attachments + Drive link below.)
2) Please confirm the POC scope: 1 endpoint, 5000 requests/day baseline, 5k token/month estimate.
3) Share a sanitized sample of 100 typical user prompts and 10 edge-case prompts (you can drop them in the Drive folder or reply to this thread).

Redwood recommendations (first pass):
- Latency-first: rw-serve-3b-8k-q (quantized) pinned to a stable release for the POC.
- Quality baseline (for classification + short text generation): rw-serve-2.0@20260625 (we recommend pinning to a release date to avoid surprise regressions during POC).

Attachments we dropped in the Drive folder: FitShot_sample_prompts.txt, fitshot_prod_flow.png. Public evaluation links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDef-FitShot-EvalPack

Please let me know if we should loop in security/compliance (we can bring our SOC2 evidence and data retention options). If that plan looks good I’ll send the benchmark CSV and a quick runbook for pinned routes.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min follow-up if useful.

--
Karthik Iyer
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0179

- Can you provide the benchmark numbers we should expect for rw-serve-3b-8k-q (p95 latency, tokens/sec, and sample cost estimate)?
- We prefer to be conservative on model churn during POC. If you recommend pinning, please include how rollback/pinning is accomplished and if it impacts throughput SLA.

I’ll upload a sanitized set of prompts by EOD tomorrow. We’ll also need your SOC2 matrix; please send that link.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Patel <nora@fitshot.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 14:40:05 -0700
Subject: Eval pack + benchmark link (FitShot POC)

Hi Nora — thanks, uploading the eval artifacts now. Links and a short runbook are below.

Drive / artifacts:
- Prompt set (sanitized): https://drive.google.com/file/d/fitshot_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (attachment: fitshot_prompt_set_v1.jsonl)
- Benchmark CSV with sample expected metrics: https://drive.google.com/file/d/fitshot_benchmarks_20260706.csv (attachment included)
- SOC2 evidence (read-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/redwood-soc2-evidence

Quick benchmarks (observed on g4dn-like instance, rw-serve-3b-8k-q):
- p50 latency (single-token batch): ~18ms
- p95 latency (typical short prompt): ~42ms
- tokens/sec (sustained, 1-request concurrency): ~120–200 depending on prompt length
- Rough cost estimate for POC: ~$0.008 per 1k tokens (ballpark; we’ll run exact numbers off your sample corpus)

Pinning & rollback notes:
- You can pin by setting the model_version at the route level (example: model_version=rw-serve-2.0@20260625). Pinning forces the route to keep serving that exact artifact until changed.
- Rollback is a single API call or Console action to change model_version to a previous tag; it does not require redeploying infra and should have negligible impact on throughput.
- If you need an automatic fallback to a cheaper variant on quota or regional outage, we can configure a routing policy that falls back to rw-serve-3b-8k-q.

Next steps I propose:
- You drop sanitized prompts in the Drive folder.
- You run the benchmark CSV or send us a sample run and we’ll score outputs and provide a small report (will highlight hallucination/label drift).

Attachments included in Drive: fitshot_prompt_set_v1.jsonl, fitshot_benchmarks_20260706.csv

Let me know if you want us to run the first benchmark on our side. We can do that and return a QA report by EOD Wednesday.

Best,
Karthik

From: Caleb Moore <caleb@fitshot.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nora Patel <nora@fitshot.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2026 09:12:28 -0700
Subject: Re: Eval pack + benchmark link (FitShot POC)

Karthik — quick update from our QA runs. We ran 250 prompts from the attached prompt set against the pinned rw-serve-2.0@20260625 baseline and then switched to the latest default route (we think it routed to rw-serve-2.0@20260701). Observations:

- ~6% of classification outputs changed label mapping (previously 'on_time' vs 'delayed', new runs show 'on_time' for cases that were previously 'delayed').
- Free-text normalization shows a small but measurable increase in hallucinated location tokens for edge-case prompts.

This is blocking our UI test — can you advise on the fastest way to get us back to the previous behavior? We want to either pin our route to the 20260625 tag or request a rollback of the default for our account. What’s the recommended approach?

Thanks,
Caleb

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nora Patel <nora@fitshot.com>, Caleb Moore <caleb@fitshot.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Regression-like diffs seen in QA — suggested immediate actions

Forwarding Caleb's QA notes. Proposed immediate plan from Redwood: 

1) Pining option (fastest for FitShot POC): we can set the route-level model_version to rw-serve-2.0@20260625 for your FitShot POC route. That will immediately restore prior behavior for all requests hitting that route. This is the low-risk path.

2) Rollback default (account-wide): if you prefer we can revert the account default to 20260625, but that is broader and we usually reserve it for escalations.

3) Triage & diff report (short term): Ben, can you run a diff report between the two builds (20260625 vs 20260701) and flag likely changes in tokenization/label mapping? If we can get the failing prompt list from FitShot (Caleb — can you mark the 15 highest-priority failures) we’ll prioritize analysis.

4) Root cause / follow-up: if the diffs are intentional model-improvement changes that affect label mapping, we’ll document the behavior change, propose a remap, and suggest regression tests the POC should add to its CI.

Ben — can you confirm ETA for the diff report? We should aim for a two-business-day turnaround. If urgent I can request acceleratated support from the SRE/model team.

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nora Patel <nora@fitshot.com>, Caleb Moore <caleb@fitshot.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2026 11:45:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Regression-like diffs seen in QA — suggested immediate actions

Agree with pin-first approach. Quick notes: 
- I’ll run a token-by-token and label-diff between rw-serve-2.0@20260625 and rw-serve-2.0@20260701. Expect an initial triage in ~6 hours, full diff report (including example prompts and suggested remap) in ~48 hours.
- Operationally, pinning at the route level is a single Console/API change and can be done immediately (no infra deploy). We’ll notify you when complete.
- If we find an upstream behavioral change that’s intentional, we’ll include recommended transformation logic (local remap table) so you can tolerate the new default without pinning forever.

Caleb/Nora: please upload the 15 highest-priority failing prompts to the Drive folder and drop a comment here with the file name you used. That will speed analysis.

Ben
Senior Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
